pages.lesson:
LESSON: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.6: Conversational skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Conversational skills. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How should one interrupt a speaker in a conversation without sounding rude?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary related to foodstuff for comprehension
2. apply etiquette and turn- taking skills in oral conversations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Conversational skills helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to a conversation about the kitchen, meal preparation and utensils used,
2. Collaborate with peers to talk about vocabulary related to kitchen items and meals, using simple descriptions,
3. Communication and Collaboration: These are enhanced as the learner speaks engagingly when collaborating with peers to talk about vocabulary related to kitchen items and meals.
4. Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner demonstrates tolerance when engaging in a dialogue using appropriate turn taking skills and interrupting politely. 12 Values:
5. Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner diligently takes up assigned roles when engaging in a dialogue using appropriate turn-taking skills and interrupting politely.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
